newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac, Kohl to confer on EU, NATO next Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Chirac, Kohl to confer on EU, NATO next Wednesday.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl and French President Jacques Chirac will hold informal talks on European Union and NATO issues over dinner in Bonn next Wednesday, the French leader's office announced on Friday.

The leaders, who meet roughly every six weeks to coordinate policies, will discuss EU reform negotiations, progress towards a single European currency, reform of the NATO defence alliance and enlargement of both the EU and NATO, French officials said.

Their meeting, beginning at 1730 GMT, will help prepare for summits in Amsterdam and Madrid which are due to complete a hard-fought overhaul of the European Union's institutions and a reform of NATO leading to the admission of the first former communist central European states.

France and Germany have taken joint positions on many of the issues but face resistance from Britain and neutral EU member states to their drive to transform the Union in stages into a fully-fledged defence alliance.
Kohl ended months of uncertainty on Thursday by announcing he would seek reelection to a record fifth term next year.
Chirac immediately praised the chancellor's "determined action" and said he looked forward to continuing to build European union with him.
